text.en: Think of your favourite food made at home. Is it sweet, sour, spicy or salty? Today we find out why we eat and drink, what makes a healthy plate, and where our food comes from.

We all like to eat and drink many different things. Some foods are sweet, some are sour, some are spicy and some are bitter. We eat fruits and vegetables, and we eat rice, dal or roti. We drink milk, lassi and juice. But why do we eat and drink at all? We can talk to the elders at home and discuss this in class. Food and water give our body the strength to play, run, study and grow.
Shirin was in class 3, and she ran faster than everyone in her class. One day at a school sports event she met a champion runner who had won many medals. Shirin asked, How can I run like you and win medals? The champion said she could also become a champion if she practised a lot and ate healthy food. Shirin said she practised a lot but often fell sick, and she only liked rice and potatoes. The champion laughed kindly. Rice and potatoes are good, but she must eat a lot of other things too, to have a strong and healthy body. Shirin followed the advice, practised harder, and after a few months she ran faster and won a medal for her school.
The champion told Shirin to eat different kinds of vegetables and fruits. She told her to eat things made from different grains like rice, ragi, jowar, wheat and bajra. She told her to eat pulses, which we call dal, and nuts. And she said that food cooked at home is always good to eat. When we eat many kinds of good food together in the right amounts, it is called a balanced diet, and Shirin understood its value.
Elders cook different foods in summer and in winter. When it is hot, we love kulfi, ice-cream and tender coconut water. In winter we like warm food, soups, stew and hot drinks. Fruits and vegetables also change with the season: mangoes and melons come in summer, and plenty of apples come in winter. Such foods are called seasonal foods, and eating them is good because they are fresh in that season. In different parts of our country people eat different delicious dishes, and we can find out the names of foods we have not tasted yet.
In summer the weather is hot and we sweat a lot. When we sweat we lose water from our body, so we must drink more water, buttermilk, lime water, aam panna, sugarcane juice or tender coconut water. We also sweat when we play or do any physical activity, so we should drink water often. Our body needs a lot of water, and we cannot live without it, which is why we say that water is life.
Some foods grow in fields, like wheat, rice and vegetables, and they are cooked in many forms. We eat different parts of plants: leaves like spinach, methi and coriander, fruits like guava and mango, and roots like carrot, radish and beetroot. We also eat stems like potato, ginger and onion, which grow under the ground, and seeds like grains, pulses and dry fruits. Some foods come from animals, such as milk, curd, ghee, cheese, paneer, honey, eggs and meat. The textbook puzzle asks for two common ingredients that come from neither plants nor animals. One of them is salt, and the other is water. Some foods use both: lassi has curd, which comes from milk, and sugar, which is made from sugarcane.
Food takes the work of many people, so we should not waste it. We can take only as much as we can eat and finish what is on our plate. We can share our food with a friend who has not brought lunch. Sharing a fruit chaat or salad with the class is a lovely way to eat together.

problem.en: Plan a day of food on three plates: morning, afternoon and night.

text.en: Morning: choose roti or idli with dal or milk and one fruit.

why.en: Grains give energy, dal and milk help the body grow, and fruit adds freshness.

text.en: Afternoon: choose rice, dal, two vegetables and a salad.

why.en: Different vegetables and rice or roti make a balanced plate.

text.en: Night: choose a light meal like roti, vegetable and curd.

why.en: A light home-cooked meal is easy to digest.

text.en: Drink water at each meal and between meals.

why.en: The body needs water, especially on hot days.

problem.en: Sort these into leaf, fruit, root, stem or seed: palak, guava, carrot, potato, rajma.

text.en: Palak is a leaf.
Guava is a fruit.

why.en: We eat the fruit of the guava tree.

text.en: Carrot is a root.

why.en: It grows below the ground as the plant's root.

text.en: Potato is a stem.

why.en: It is an underground stem, like ginger and onion.

text.en: Rajma is a seed.

why.en: Pulses and grains are seeds of plants.

problem.en: A guest comes home suddenly. What do you serve and why?

text.en: Offer water or lime water first.
Serve a simple home-cooked meal with some vegetables, dal or roti.

why.en: Home-cooked food is healthy and balanced.

text.en: Add a fruit or something sweet.

why.en: It makes the meal special and welcoming.

prompt.en: Tell a friend why Shirin became faster and what a balanced plate means.

requiredIdeas.en: Shirin ate many kinds of healthy home-cooked food, not only rice and potatoes
A balanced diet has grains, vegetables, fruits, pulses and milk products
We drink water often, especially when it is hot or when we play
Foods come from plants and animals, and we should not waste them

commonMisconceptions.en: Eating only our favourite food is enough
Water is needed only in summer

points.en: We eat and drink to get strength to play, run, study and grow.
A balanced diet means many kinds of healthy food: grains, vegetables, fruits, pulses, nuts and milk products.
Seasonal foods are fresh in their season, and we drink more water when it is hot.
We eat leaves, fruits, roots, stems and seeds of plants, and milk, eggs and honey from animals.
We should share food and not waste it.
